title: Lamport ordered events without trusting any clock
body: Physical clocks in different machines can never be perfectly synchronised, so Lamport's 1978 logical clocks count causality instead: if A happened before B, A's counter is smaller, enforced by carrying counters in messages. Distributed debugging, version vectors and even Git's sense of ancestry live downstream of asking 'what could have caused what' instead of 'what time is it'.
source_hint: Lamport, 'Time, Clocks, and the Ordering of Events' (1978)
